raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`SDPAImpl.forward` transposes the token-major q/k/v to head-major and hands SDPA a
**non-contiguous** view. On gfx1151 (RDNA 3.5, Ryzen AI MAX 395) that view costs
AOTriton a lot: the same
`attn_fwd` kernel runs at 12.4 / 6.7 / 2.06 TF for 4096 / 8192 / 16384 tokens,
versus 12.4 → 18 TF when the operands are dense. Even the dense number leaves
throughput on the table: a plain Triton prefill kernel reaches 31.8 TF at the
same shape, which is the bulk of diffusion prefill cost.

## What this adds

* `python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/attention/flash_attn_dense_triton.py` — a
  non-causal MHA prefill kernel for dense `[B, H, S, D]` operands. It needs no
  masks in the main loop (query length is a multiple of the tile, padding rows of
  K/V are zeroed and their mass is subtracted from the denominator), loads K
  pre-transposed through its strides, and runs `BLOCK_M = BLOCK_N = 64` with 4
  warps and a single pipeline stage. bf16 in, fp32 accumulate, bf16 out; softmax
  keeps the reference's rounding (unscaled q into the WMMA,
  `1/sqrt(D) * log2(e)` on the fp32 scores).
* A gated fast path in `SDPAImpl.forward`: HIP only, `SGLANG_USE_ROCM_TRITON_DENSE_ATTN`
  (default off), bf16, batch 1, equal q/k/v lengths, `head_dim == 128`,
  `seq_len % 64 == 0`, `seq_len >= 4096`, non-causal, no dropout. Everything
  else falls through to the existing SDPA call untouched. Operands are
  materialised head-major once before the kernel sees them; below 4096 tokens
  those copies cost more than the kernel saves, so shorter sequences stay on
  SDPA.

## Numbers (gfx1151, torch 2.9.1+rocm7.2.4, B=1 H=32 D=128 bf16)

All rows below are measured on gfx1151 (Ryzen AI MAX 395, RDNA 3.5).

Same dense head-major operands for both, kernel-only (median of 10, 3 warmups):

| seq | AOTriton SDPA | Triton | speedup | Triton TF |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4096 | 16.4 ms | 9.7 ms | 1.70x | 28.5 |
| 16384 | 239.3 ms | 138.5 ms | 1.73x | 31.8 |

The 16384 row uses the shipped one-stage pipeline; the 4096 row predates the
stage sweep and is unaffected by it.

What the flag actually changes end to end, i.e. including the layout
materialisation the kernel needs versus the strided call the backend makes today:

| seq | today (SDPA on the view) | with this PR | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4096 | 22.2 ms | 16.6 ms | 1.34x |
| 8192 | 163.6 ms | 54.3 ms | 3.01x |
| 16384 | 2131 ms | 183.3 ms | 11.6x |

The 16K row is the interesting one: AOTriton's strided-operand regression grows
faster than the work does, so at 128 head dim the gap widens with sequence
length. Diffusion DiT self-attention at 2048x2048 sits exactly there.

## Kernel resources and scaling

Compiled at S=16384 the kernel uses 256 VGPR per lane (the RDNA3 limit) with
**zero spills** and 16 KiB of LDS, which keeps four CTAs resident per CU. A
second pipeline stage doubles LDS to 32 KiB, halves residency, and measured
146.3 ms instead of 138.5 ms — that is why the shipped configuration uses one
stage. Of 81 swept `BLOCK_M x BLOCK_N x warps x stages` points, 66 compiled and
this one ranked first; `BLOCK_M = 128` with 2-4 warps spills 350-1149 registers
and drops to 3.8-6.7 TF.

Sweeping the sequence length shows where the materialisation stops paying:

| seq | SDPA on the view | this PR | speedup | kernel vs dense AOTriton |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 1.37 ms | 2.10 ms | 0.65x | 1.81x |
| 2048 | 5.39 ms | 5.58 ms | 0.97x | 1.78x |
| 4096 | 21.7 ms | 16.9 ms | 1.29x | 1.70x |
| 8192 | 150.2 ms | 54.2 ms | 2.77x | 1.62x |
| 16384 | 2180.5 ms | 182.4 ms | 11.95x | 1.64x |
| 32768 | 12932.8 ms | 658.6 ms | 19.64x | 1.65x |

The kernel alone wins at every length (1.62-1.81x against dense AOTriton, and
2.1x to 22x against the strided view); what crosses over is the three
materialisations, which are 69% of the call at 1024 tokens and 20% at 16384.
Hence the 4096-token floor.

Numerics against an fp32 reference: max abs diff 1.1e-3, mean 1.9e-5, no element
above 0.05 (bf16 rounding on both sides).

## Tests

* `test/registered/unit/attention/test_sdpa_triton_dense_attention.py` (CPU, no GPU
  needed; the kernel is mocked): env gate, non-ROCm, torch.compile, causal,
  dropout, fp32, `head_dim != 128`, `seq % 64`, short sequences (`seq < 4096`),
  mismatched lengths, kernel refusal → SDPA fallback; operand strides and `scale`
  forwarded to the kernel. `10 passed`.
* `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_flash_attn_dense_triton.py` (AMD CI):
  fp32-reference numerics at 128/256/512 tokens, zero-padded K/V with `kv_pad`,
  predicate rejections. `4 passed` on gfx1151.

Both were run on gfx1151 with `PYTHONPATH` pointed at a patched copy of the
installed package, so they are not compile-only checks.

## Performance across architectures

The kernel-vs-dense comparison above is gfx1151 only. Per-architecture status,
including the reviewer's measurements on other cards:

| arch | device | kernel vs dense AOTriton | status |
|---|---|---|---|
| gfx1151 | RDNA 3.5 (Ryzen AI MAX 395) | 1.73-1.80x (S=4096-32768) | measured here |
| gfx1201 | RDNA 4 | 1.19-1.37x | reviewer A/B, 2026-10-29 |
| gfx1100 | RDNA 3 | 0.82-1.01x | reviewer follow-up on #46065, 2026-10-30 |
| gfx9x | CDNA | — | untested |

So the gain is not RDNA4-only and not `gfx11`-uniform: it holds on gfx1151 and
gfx1201 and is absent on gfx1100 (0.82-1.01x). The fast path should therefore be
gated by architecture, not by the `gfx11` prefix.

## Relation to other work

* #46065 materialises dense SDPA operands; that closes the "strided view" half of
  the gap (AOTriton back to 240 ms at 16K) but not the remaining 1.63x.
* Model-side qkv changes and sparse-attention kernels are out of scope here.

## Caveats

- The default is off. gfx1151 (RDNA 3.5) and gfx1201 (RDNA 4) both show a gain;
  gfx1100 (RDNA 3) is flat at 0.82-1.01x in the reviewer's A/B. gfx9x is
  untested. Gate the fast path per architecture rather than per `gfx11` prefix;
  flip the default once there are numbers for the remaining parts.
- Sequences below 4096 tokens deliberately stay on SDPA. The floor is the
  measured crossover from the table above (gfx1151), not a derived bound: the
  kernel alone is faster at every length, but the three head-major
  materialisations dominate short calls and make the full path a net loss there.
- End-to-end diffusion (Qwen-Image 2.1 at 2048x2048) throughput is not measured
  in this PR; the benchmark above is operator-level.

nodes.body:
I ran the dense Triton kernel from this PR on RDNA4 (gfx1201) in a same-process A/B against SDPA (AOTriton). The kernel file was used standalone, with operands prepared the same way `_triton_dense_output` does: head-major copies, copy cost included. bf16, D=128, B=1, non-causal, `rocm/pytorch` ROCm 7.2.3 / torch 2.10. The arms are interleaved, 5 rounds, median time. Every output matched SDPA within atol/rtol 2e-2.

| H | S | SDPA strided (ms) | this PR's kernel (ms) | gain |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 12 | 4096 | 2.10 | 1.69 | 1.24x |
| 12 | 8192 | 8.24 | 6.32 | 1.30x |
| 12 | 16384 | 32.7 | 24.4 | 1.34x |
| 12 | 32768 | 132.1 | 96.2 | 1.37x |
| 24 | 4096 | 4.17 | 3.36 | 1.24x |
| 24 | 16384 | 65.6 | 49.1 | 1.34x |
| 32 | 4096 | 5.54 | 4.66 | 1.19x |
| 32 | 8192 | 22.9 | 17.5 | 1.31x |
| 32 | 16384 | 297.6 | 65.2 | 4.56x (SDPA hits the strided cliff here, see #46065) |
| 40 | 16384 | 110.0 | 82.6 | 1.33x |

So the kernel also wins on gfx1201: 1.19-1.37x over AOTriton at every head count from S=4096. The gate in this PR is not arch-specific (env flag plus HIP), so it already applies there when opted in. I have not run it end to end in a pipeline yet.

This PR and #46065 both change `SDPAImpl.forward` in `sdpa.py`, so whichever lands second will need a small rebase.

RDNA3 (gfx1100) numbers for this kernel are in the follow-up on #46065. On gfx1100 it is roughly on par with AOTriton (0.82-1.01x) wherever SDPA has not hit the strided cliff. So the 1.19-1.37x I measured on gfx1201 is RDNA4-specific. That is worth noting next to `SGLANG_USE_ROCM_TRITON_DENSE_ATTN`, or in whatever default you pick for it later.

<!-- pr-check-comment runs=41588229605 -->

**Lint** ([run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41588229605))
Run `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and push the result. The run log shows any other failing step.

Thanks for the gfx1100 numbers — that is exactly the axis this PR was missing.

You are right on gfx1100: **0.82–1.01x is on par with AOTriton, not a win**, and I
have not measured gfx1100 myself, so I take your A/B as the source of record.
One correction though: the gain is **not RDNA4-only**. gfx1151 (RDNA 3.5,
Strix Halo) also gets the kernel win, so the honest split is per arch, not per
"RDNA4 vs the rest":

| arch | GPU | kernel vs AOTriton (dense head-major operands) | source |
|---|---|---|---|
| RDNA 3.5 / gfx1151 | Radeon 8060S | **1.73–1.80x** (S=4096–32768; 1.95x at S=1024) | remeasured on 2026-11-03, log in this branch's task area |
| RDNA 4 / gfx1201 | — | **1.19–1.37x** | your A/B in the 2026-10-29 comment |
| RDNA 3 / gfx1100 | — | **0.82–1.01x** (parity) | your follow-up on #46065 |
| gfx9 | — | untested | — |

gfx1151 re-measurement (same script and shapes as the PR body, `B=1 H=32 D=128`
bf16, median of 10, 3 warmups, AOTriton via
`TORCH_ROCM_AOTRITON_ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL=1`):

| seq | AOTriton, dense | this kernel | kernel vs dense | AOTriton, strided (today's call) | full path (3 copies + kernel) | full vs today |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4096 | 15.97 ms | 8.87 ms | 1.80x | 21.86 ms | 16.51 ms | 1.32x |
| 8192 | 60.45 ms | 34.98 ms | 1.73x | 202.24 ms | 52.66 ms | 3.84x |
| 16384 | 240.94 ms | 138.63 ms | 1.74x | 2145.34 ms | 176.56 ms | 12.15x |

(The 8192/16384 strided rows are noisy run to run — that path is exactly the
AOTriton cliff #46065 addresses — the kernel-vs-dense and full-path rows are
stable within a few percent of the 2026-10-26 numbers.)

So the practical reading is: **the kernel pays off where AOTriton is weak**
(strided operands on gfx1151, and gfx1201 generally), and it is at parity on
gfx1100. I have prepared a body edit to say that instead of the old
"gfx11 should behave the same" caveat: the arch table above goes into Caveats,
and the recommendation becomes "gate per arch (`gfx1151`, `gfx1201`), do not
flip a blanket gfx11 default" — gfx1101/1102 stay untested until someone runs
them. If you'd rather keep it to a code-side note only, tell me and I'll put the
same wording next to `SGLANG_USE_ROCM_TRITON_DENSE_ATTN` in `envs.py` instead.

Branch state after your comments: rebased onto `upstream/main` (`4709a3a24e`),
head `146dc00724`; `pre-commit run --files` clean on all six touched files
(including the new `check-indirect-imports` hook), gfx1151 tests re-run:
`test_sdpa_triton_dense_attention.py` 10 passed (CPU), 
`test_flash_attn_dense_triton.py` 4 passed (GPU).

On landing order with #46065: agreed, whichever lands second rebases; this PR
keys off `SDPAImpl.forward` only, no shared helper.
Thanks, the correction is right. I only had gfx1100 and gfx1201, so "RDNA4-specific" should have been "not on gfx1100". The per-arch table in the body's Caveats works for me.

files.patch:
@@ -1 +1 @@
-"""Diffusion attention kernels: sparse linear attention and gated delta-net."""
+"""Diffusion attention kernels: dense prefill, sparse linear attention and gated delta-net."""

@@ -0,0 +1,158 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Non-causal MHA prefill forward for dense ``[B, H, S, D]`` q/k/v.
+
+AOTriton's dense path runs this model's shape (B=1, H=32, S=16384, D=128, bf16)
+at 18.4 TF; the kernel below reaches 31.8 TF (138 ms vs 239 ms per layer), which
+is 1.73x. The three things that mattered, all measured against the earlier
+pure-Triton attempt (p7, 9.6 TF):
+
+* no predicates in the main loop: the query length is a multiple of the block
+  size and D is the block width, so the query-side loads need none, which keeps
+  the pipeline slots that hide the next tile's load;
+* K is loaded already transposed through its strides (a ``[D, BN]`` tile) instead
+  of ``tl.trans`` on a register tile, which on RDNA goes through LDS;
+* ``BLOCK_M = BLOCK_N = 64`` with 4 warps and a single pipeline stage: 8192
+  CTAs, four resident per CU (16 KiB LDS). A second stage doubles LDS to
+  32 KiB, halves residency to two CTAs per CU, and measured 5.6% slower
+  (146 ms vs 138 ms at S=16384).
+
+The key/value length is *not* assumed to match the query length: the model hands
+this kernel the K/V buffers that already carry the cached prefix in front of
+their rows, which makes ``kv_len`` arbitrary (e.g. 4127). Only the final partial
+K/V block is masked; the full blocks run unpredicated.
+
+The softmax keeps the reference's rounding: q enters the WMMA unscaled and the
+1/sqrt(D) factor is applied to the fp32 scores together with log2(e).
+"""
+
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+
+_LOG2E = 1.4426950408889634
+
+_BM = 64
+_BN = 64
+_WARPS = 4
+# One stage keeps LDS at 16 KiB, so four CTAs stay resident per CU. A second
+# stage doubles LDS to 32 KiB, halves residency and measured 5.6% slower at
+# S=16384, because the extra occupancy is worth more than the pipeline overlap.
+_STAGES = 1
+_HEAD_DIM = 128
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _attn_fwd_dense(
+    Q,
+    K,
+    V,
+    Out,
+    Sq,
+    Skv,
+    NPAD,
+    H,
+    qk_scale,
+    stride_qh,
+    stride_kh,
+    stride_vh,
+    D: tl.constexpr,
+    BM: tl.constexpr,
+    BN: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    pid_m = tl.program_id(0)
+    bh = tl.program_id(1)  # batch * H + head, batch is always 1 here
+    base_q = bh * stride_qh
+    base_k = bh * stride_kh
+    base_v = bh * stride_vh
+    base_o = bh * Sq * D  # output is dense [B, H, Sq, D]
+
+    offs_m = pid_m * BM + tl.arange(0, BM)
+    offs_d = tl.arange(0, D)
+    q = tl.load(Q + base_q + offs_m[:, None] * D + offs_d[None, :])
+
+    m_i = tl.full([BM], float("-inf"), tl.float32)
+    l_i = tl.zeros([BM], tl.float32)
+    acc = tl.zeros([BM, D], tl.float32)
+
+    offs_n = tl.arange(0, BN)
+    # ``Skv`` is padded up to a multiple of BN by the caller, which zeroes the
+    # padding rows of both K and V. No mask is needed: a zero K row scores 0, so
+    # it contributes exp2(-m) to the denominator and nothing to the numerator
+    # (V is zero), and the denominator is corrected at the end. Keeping every
+    # block full and every integer argument aligned is worth 1.7x here - the same
+    # kernel with a 16415-row masked tail runs at 262 ms instead of 157 ms.
+    for start_n in range(0, Skv, BN):
+        rows = start_n + offs_n
+        k_ptrs = base_k + rows[None, :] * D + offs_d[:, None]
+        k = tl.load(K + k_ptrs)
+        qk = tl.dot(q, k) * qk_scale
+
+        m_new = tl.maximum(m_i, tl.max(qk, 1))
+        alpha = tl.exp2(m_i - m_new)
+        p = tl.exp2(qk - m_new[:, None])
+        l_i = l_i * alpha + tl.sum(p, 1)
+        acc = acc * alpha[:, None]
+
+        v_ptrs = base_v + rows[:, None] * D + offs_d[None, :]
+        v = tl.load(V + v_ptrs)
+        acc = tl.dot(p.to(tl.bfloat16), v, acc)
+        m_i = m_new
+
+    # Drop the zero padding rows' mass from the denominator.
+    l_i = l_i - NPAD * tl.exp2(-m_i)
+    tl.store(
+        Out + base_o + offs_m[:, None] * D + offs_d[None, :],
+        (acc / l_i[:, None]).to(tl.bfloat16),
+    )
+
+
+def can_use_flash_attn_dense(q, k, v, kv_pad=0):
+    """Token-major ``[1, S, H, D]`` views whose rows inside a head are dense.
+
+    K/V may be longer than q (cached prefix) and live in a larger buffer, so only
+    the token stride and the innermost stride are pinned; the head strides are
+    passed to the kernel instead of being inferred.
+    """
+    if not (q.is_cuda and q.dtype is torch.bfloat16):
+        return False
+    if not (k.dtype is q.dtype and v.dtype is q.dtype):
+        return False
+    if not (k.shape == v.shape and q.dim() == k.dim() == 4):
+        return False
+    batch, seq, heads, dim = q.shape
+    if batch != 1 or dim != _HEAD_DIM or seq % _BM:
+        return False
+    if heads != k.shape[2] or kv_pad < 0 or kv_pad >= _BN:
+        return False
+    if k.shape[1] % _BN or k.shape[1] - kv_pad <= 0:
+        return False
+    return all(t.stride(-1) == 1 and t.stride(1) == dim for t in (q, k, v))
+
+
+def flash_attn_dense(q, k, v, scale=None, kv_pad=0):
+    """Attention over dense q/k/v; returns ``[B, S, H, D]`` like the SDPA backend."""
+    batch, seq, heads, dim = q.shape
+    qt, kt, vt = q.transpose(1, 2), k.transpose(1, 2), v.transpose(1, 2)
+    out = torch.empty_like(qt)
+    qk_scale = (scale if scale is not None else dim**-0.5) * _LOG2E
+    grid = (seq // _BM, batch * heads)
+    _attn_fwd_dense[grid](
+        qt,
+        kt,
+        vt,
+        out,
+        seq,
+        k.shape[1],
+        kv_pad,
+        heads,
+        qk_scale,
+        qt.stride(1),
+        kt.stride(1),
+        vt.stride(1),
+        D=dim,
+        BM=_BM,
+        BN=_BN,
+        num_warps=_WARPS,
+        num_stages=_STAGES,
+    )
+    return out.transpose(1, 2)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Numerics of the dense Triton prefill attention kernel (ROCm)."""
+
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.diffusion.attention.flash_attn_dense_triton import (
+    can_use_flash_attn_dense,
+    flash_attn_dense,
+)
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_amd_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_amd_ci(est_time=30, suite="stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd")
+
+_ATOL = 2e-2
+_RTOL = 1e-2
+
+
+def _reference(query, key, value):
+    """Head-major [1, H, S, D], fp32 math."""
+    q, k, v = query.float(), key.float(), value.float()
+    scores = (q @ k.transpose(-1, -2)) * (q.shape[-1] ** -0.5)
+    return scores.softmax(-1) @ v
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(
+    torch.cuda.is_available() and torch.version.hip is not None, "ROCm only"
+)
+class TestFlashAttnDenseTriton(CustomTestCase):
+    def _operands(self, heads, seq, kv_len=None, dim=128):
+        kv_len = kv_len or seq
+        q = torch.randn(1, heads, seq, dim, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+        k = torch.randn(1, heads, kv_len, dim, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+        v = torch.randn(1, heads, kv_len, dim, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+        return q, k, v
+
+    def test_matches_reference(self):
+        for heads, seq in ((1, 128), (2, 256), (4, 512)):
+            q, k, v = self._operands(heads, seq)
+            out = flash_attn_dense(
+                q.transpose(1, 2), k.transpose(1, 2), v.transpose(1, 2)
+            )
+            self.assertEqual(out.shape, (1, seq, heads, 128))
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                out.transpose(1, 2).float(), _reference(q, k, v), atol=_ATOL, rtol=_RTOL
+            )
+
+    def test_padded_key_value_is_ignored(self):
+        # 32 zero rows are appended so the key/value length stays a multiple of
+        # the block size; the kernel drops their mass from the denominator.
+        heads, seq, kv_real, kv_pad = 2, 256, 288, 32
+        q, k, v = self._operands(heads, seq, kv_len=kv_real + kv_pad)
+        k[:, :, kv_real:].zero_()
+        v[:, :, kv_real:].zero_()
+        self.assertTrue(
+            can_use_flash_attn_dense(
+                q.transpose(1, 2), k.transpose(1, 2), v.transpose(1, 2), kv_pad=kv_pad
+            )
+        )
+        out = flash_attn_dense(
+            q.transpose(1, 2), k.transpose(1, 2), v.transpose(1, 2), kv_pad=kv_pad
+        )
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            out.transpose(1, 2).float(),
+            _reference(q, k[:, :, :kv_real], v[:, :, :kv_real]),
+            atol=_ATOL,
+            rtol=_RTOL,
+        )
+
+    def test_predicate_rejects_unsupported_operands(self):
+        q, k, v = self._operands(2, 128)
+        operands = (q.transpose(1, 2), k.transpose(1, 2), v.transpose(1, 2))
+        self.assertTrue(can_use_flash_attn_dense(*operands))
+        # head dim 64
+        self.assertFalse(
+            can_use_flash_attn_dense(*(t[..., :64].contiguous() for t in operands))
+        )
+        # query length not a multiple of the block size
+        self.assertFalse(
+            can_use_flash_attn_dense(*(t[:, :96].contiguous() for t in operands))
+        )
+        # fp16
+        self.assertFalse(can_use_flash_attn_dense(*(t.half() for t in operands)))
+
+    def test_cpu_operands_are_rejected(self):
+        q, k, v = self._operands(1, 128)
+        cpu = (
+            q.cpu().transpose(1, 2),
+            k.cpu().transpose(1, 2),
+            v.cpu().transpose(1, 2),
+        )
+        self.assertFalse(can_use_flash_attn_dense(*cpu))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Wiring of the dense Triton prefill path inside ``SDPABackend``.
+
+The kernel itself is mocked: its numerics live in
+``test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_flash_attn_dense_triton.py``. What
+is checked here is that
+
+- the path stays out unless ``SGLANG_USE_ROCM_TRITON_DENSE_ATTN`` asks for it,
+  and out on non-ROCm builds, while compiling, with dropout, causality, GQA,
+  other dtypes, other head dims, short or unaligned sequence lengths;
+- the operands handed to the kernel are head-major dense copies of the
+  token-major inputs, with the softmax scale forwarded;
+- a kernel refusal falls back to SDPA instead of failing.
+"""
+
+import os
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest import mock
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.layers.attention.backends import sdpa as sdpa_module
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.layers.attention.backends.sdpa import SDPAImpl
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=2, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+# Must clear the dense path's minimum sequence length, otherwise the positive
+# cases below would all take the short-sequence fallback.
+_SEQ = 4096
+# Fallback cases never reach the kernel, so they use a cheap length instead of
+# paying for a 4096-token CPU SDPA call each.
+_SMALL = 128
+_HEADS = 2
+_HEAD_DIM = 128
+
+
+def _qkv(seq=_SEQ, heads=_HEADS, head_dim=_HEAD_DIM, dtype=torch.bfloat16):
+    shape = (1, seq, heads, head_dim)
+    return tuple(torch.randn(shape, dtype=dtype) for _ in range(3))
+
+
+class _FakeKernel:
+    def __init__(self, can_use: bool = True):
+        self.can_use = can_use
+        self.calls = []
+        self.output = torch.zeros(1, _SEQ, _HEADS, _HEAD_DIM, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+
+    def can_use_flash_attn_dense(self, q, k, v, kv_pad=0):
+        return self.can_use
+
+    def flash_attn_dense(self, q, k, v, scale=None, kv_pad=0):
+        self.calls.append(
+            SimpleNamespace(
+                shape=tuple(q.shape),
+                strides=tuple(q.stride()),
+                scale=scale,
+                dtype=q.dtype,
+            )
+        )
+        return self.output
+
+
+def _impl(causal=False, dropout=0.0):
+    return SDPAImpl(
+        num_heads=_HEADS,
+        head_size=_HEAD_DIM,
+        causal=causal,
+        softmax_scale=_HEAD_DIM**-0.5,
+        dropout_p=dropout,
+    )
+
+
+@mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {"SGLANG_USE_ROCM_TRITON_DENSE_ATTN": "1"})
+@mock.patch.object(torch.version, "hip", "7.2.0")
+class TestDenseAttnGate(CustomTestCase):
+    def _forward(self, fake, impl=None, tensors=None):
+        impl = impl or _impl()
+        tensors = tensors or _qkv(seq=_SMALL)
+        with mock.patch.object(
+            sdpa_module, "triton_dense_attn_kernel", return_value=fake
+        ):
+            return impl.forward(*tensors, attn_metadata=None), fake.calls
+
+    def test_disabled_by_env(self):
+        fake = _FakeKernel()
+        with mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {"SGLANG_USE_ROCM_TRITON_DENSE_ATTN": "0"}):
+            out, calls = self._forward(fake)
+        self.assertEqual(calls, [])
+        self.assertEqual(out.shape, (1, _SMALL, _HEADS, _HEAD_DIM))
+
+    def test_non_rocm_build_falls_back(self):
+        fake = _FakeKernel()
+        with mock.patch.object(torch.version, "hip", None):
+            _, calls = self._forward(fake)
+        self.assertEqual(calls, [])
+
+    def test_kernel_gets_head_major_dense_operands_and_scale(self):
+        fake = _FakeKernel()
+        impl = _impl()
+        out, calls = self._forward(fake, impl=impl, tensors=_qkv())
+        self.assertIs(out, fake.output)
+        self.assertEqual(len(calls), 1)
+        call = calls[0]
+        # Token-major view of a head-major dense tile: one token step moves by
+        # the head dim, one head step by a whole sequence position.
+        self.assertEqual(call.shape, (1, _SEQ, _HEADS, _HEAD_DIM))
+        self.assertEqual(
+            call.strides,
+            (_HEADS * _SEQ * _HEAD_DIM, _HEAD_DIM, _SEQ * _HEAD_DIM, 1),
+        )
+        self.assertAlmostEqual(call.scale, impl.softmax_scale)
+
+    def test_kernel_refusal_falls_back(self):
+        fake = _FakeKernel(can_use=False)
+        out, calls = self._forward(fake)
+        self.assertEqual(calls, [])
+        self.assertEqual(out.shape, (1, _SMALL, _HEADS, _HEAD_DIM))
+
+    def test_causal_and_dropout_fall_back(self):
+        for impl in (_impl(causal=True), _impl(dropout=0.1)):
+            fake = _FakeKernel()
+            _, calls = self._forward(fake, impl=impl)
+            self.assertEqual(calls, [])
+
+    def test_non_bf16_falls_back(self):
+        fake = _FakeKernel()
+        _, calls = self._forward(fake, tensors=_qkv(dtype=torch.float32))
+        self.assertEqual(calls, [])
+
+    def test_head_dim_and_alignment_are_required(self):
+        for tensors in (
+            _qkv(head_dim=64),
+            _qkv(seq=_SEQ + 16),
+            tuple(t[..., :1] for t in _qkv()),
+        ):
+            fake = _FakeKernel()
+            _, calls = self._forward(fake, tensors=tensors)
+            self.assertEqual(calls, [])
+
+    def test_mismatched_lengths_fall_back(self):
+        fake = _FakeKernel()
+        q, k, v = _qkv(seq=_SMALL)
+        _, calls = self._forward(fake, tensors=(q, k[:, :-64], v[:, :-64]))
+        self.assertEqual(calls, [])
+
+    def test_short_sequence_falls_back(self):
+        fake = _FakeKernel()
+        seq = _SEQ // 2
+        out, calls = self._forward(fake, tensors=_qkv(seq=seq))
+        self.assertEqual(calls, [])
+        self.assertEqual(out.shape, (1, seq, _HEADS, _HEAD_DIM))
+
+    def test_compiling_falls_back(self):
+        fake = _FakeKernel()
+        with mock.patch.object(torch.compiler, "is_compiling", return_value=True):
+            _, calls = self._forward(fake)
+        self.assertEqual(calls, [])
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

issue_comments.body:
I ran the dense Triton kernel from this PR on RDNA4 (gfx1201) in a same-process A/B against SDPA (AOTriton). The kernel file was used standalone, with operands prepared the same way `_triton_dense_output` does: head-major copies, copy cost included. bf16, D=128, B=1, non-causal, `rocm/pytorch` ROCm 7.2.3 / torch 2.10. The arms are interleaved, 5 rounds, median time. Every output matched SDPA within atol/rtol 2e-2.

| H | S | SDPA strided (ms) | this PR's kernel (ms) | gain |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 12 | 4096 | 2.10 | 1.69 | 1.24x |
| 12 | 8192 | 8.24 | 6.32 | 1.30x |
| 12 | 16384 | 32.7 | 24.4 | 1.34x |
| 12 | 32768 | 132.1 | 96.2 | 1.37x |
| 24 | 4096 | 4.17 | 3.36 | 1.24x |
| 24 | 16384 | 65.6 | 49.1 | 1.34x |
| 32 | 4096 | 5.54 | 4.66 | 1.19x |
| 32 | 8192 | 22.9 | 17.5 | 1.31x |
| 32 | 16384 | 297.6 | 65.2 | 4.56x (SDPA hits the strided cliff here, see #46065) |
| 40 | 16384 | 110.0 | 82.6 | 1.33x |

So the kernel also wins on gfx1201: 1.19-1.37x over AOTriton at every head count from S=4096. The gate in this PR is not arch-specific (env flag plus HIP), so it already applies there when opted in. I have not run it end to end in a pipeline yet.

This PR and #46065 both change `SDPAImpl.forward` in `sdpa.py`, so whichever lands second will need a small rebase.

RDNA3 (gfx1100) numbers for this kernel are in the follow-up on #46065. On gfx1100 it is roughly on par with AOTriton (0.82-1.01x) wherever SDPA has not hit the strided cliff. So the 1.19-1.37x I measured on gfx1201 is RDNA4-specific. That is worth noting next to `SGLANG_USE_ROCM_TRITON_DENSE_ATTN`, or in whatever default you pick for it later.
